title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Tuesday evening, Nov 24
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 5:20 PM ET Tuesday, Nov 24, 2026. Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). New and on top: '38 million invalid voters — do not certify,' a Joe Hoft blog figure that its own source calls records 'flagged for further investigation': 47,441 posts in 24 hours, 3.14× its prior daily average, the largest query in the set. The Newsom death-row attack kept climbing (9,351 posts, up from 8,000 this morning; 3,133 from 7 AM to 5 PM ET versus 1,773 the same hours Monday) as 14 Republican attorneys general piled on. Also new on the Right: 'The T in Texas is for trans,' a gala clip amplified by Alabama Gov.-elect Tommy Tuberville (2,926 posts, 10.48×). The Michigan Wi-Fi claim (9,715) and the forensic-audit demand (12,007) cooled in daytime hours. On the Far Left, Medicare for All is still the second-largest query (12,372) but below its weekly average, and the Van Hollen push got a celebrity letter (De Niro, Fonda) while posting cooled (3,642). Two faded cards were dropped and two were added. Every count, quote and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this evening or carried over from this morning and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

Political names included 'Blanche' (30,520), 'Rudy Giuliani' (15,911) and 'Presidential Medal of Freedom' (12,932), after Trump gave Giuliani the medal, plus 'Unclassified' (8,516), 'Boston City Council' (2,471), 'CIA and ODNI' and 'America's Mayor' (no counts). None matched a card in this set, so no card gets the trend bonus this evening. 'Newscum,' on the list this morning, was not. oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. The new 'do not certify' card is tagged Right because it seeks to block results Democrats won. The new Texas card is tagged Right because it uses an activist's speech to brand the incoming Democratic state government. The Newsom death-row card is tagged Right because it is the administration's attack on a Democratic governor and potential 2028 candidate. The Rikers card is a Right attack on a Democratic mayor; we include it because Mamdani is being used as the national face of the party. The 'fine people' card is tagged Right because it uses a Fox co-host's comment to brand Democrats as liars; it is about a 2017 quote, not the midterms. The Michigan Wi-Fi and audit cards are tagged Right because they cast doubt on elections Democrats won. The Somali–Minnesota card is tagged Right because it is Trump's attack on a community in a Democratic-run state. The tax card is tagged Right because 'Democrats will raise your taxes' is the Right's reading of a hearings plan; no bill exists yet. The Medicare for All card is tagged Far Left because the pressure is on Jeffries, Schumer and the incoming majority to deliver it now. The Van Hollen card is tagged Far Left because the push to replace Schumer comes from the party's left. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Tuesday, Nov 24, 2026, 5:20 PM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API, and it will go stale. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 5:13 PM ET. This morning's snapshot (Nov 24, 7:20 AM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. Nine of its eleven narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps this morning's by 14 hours (5 PM Monday to 7 AM Tuesday ET), so we also report each query's 7 AM–5 PM ET daytime count against the same hours Monday. Two narratives were dropped because they faded: the Rubio 'democratic socialism is Marxism' card (1,111 posts in the last 24 hours, down from 3,317 this morning; 175 from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Tuesday versus 2,381 the same hours Monday) and the 'Democrats crashed the market' card (1,837 posts, 0.33× its prior daily average, down from 3,746 this morning; 762 in Tuesday's daytime hours versus 2,662 Monday). Two were added with new queries: 'do not certify / 38 million invalid voters' and 'the T in Texas is for trans.' Other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: the resurfaced attack on NYC chief counsel Ramzi Kassem for once defending an al-Qaeda defendant (2,272 posts in 24 hours, up from about 19 a day, but 1,743 of them overnight and 529 in Tuesday's daytime hours; Mamdani named him in December 2025 per Fox News and the New York Post, and City & State has reported the defense), Rep. Sarah McBride's financial-deregulation votes (204 posts on the UTC day of Nov 24) and progressive objections to Pallone and Neal (15 posts over seven days). Trump's Presidential Medal of Freedom for Rudy Giuliani trended (15,911 posts) and a Giuliani-plus-medal query matched 10,562 posts on the UTC day of Nov 24, but it is not an opposition narrative about Democrats, so it has no card.

For each narrative we ran one English-language X search with x.get_posts_counts_recent twice: at daily granularity over a 167-hour window from 6:00 PM ET Tuesday, Nov 17, through 5:00 PM ET Tuesday, Nov 24 (the 'seven-day' total), and at hourly granularity from 7:00 AM ET Monday, Nov 23, through 5:00 PM ET Tuesday, Nov 24. The last 24 of those hours (5:00 PM ET Monday through 5:00 PM ET Tuesday) are the 24-hour count; the first ten give the Monday daytime comparison. The Newsom card's Monday daytime figure (1,773) comes from this morning's hourly pull. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved and cite on the card. Official government pages, congressional offices, transcripts, advocacy groups, blogs, aggregators, archives, X News summaries and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets; this evening that includes Joe Hoft's blog, Unite4Freedom, The Watering Hole, Wisevoter and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries' office. This evening we researched the two new cards and re-researched the Newsom, Van Hollen, Medicare for All, audit and Michigan Wi-Fi cards; the 'fine people,' Rikers, tax and Somali–Minnesota cards carry this morning's outlet counts and say so. No topic in this set was on the U.S. trends list at about 5:13 PM ET.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list when we pulled it. No card got the trend bonus this evening; the Newsom card lost the bonus it had this morning. The Newsom, Michigan Wi-Fi and Texas queries had small baselines earlier in the week, so their acceleration indexes are maxed out. The 'do not certify' query carried 4,000–18,000 posts a day earlier in the week, so its 3.14× is from a large base. Morning-to-evening score changes also reflect the volume ceiling (47,441 this evening versus 16,901 this morning), which lowers every other card's volume index, and how much coverage we retrieved. Read the post counts alongside the scores.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The 'do not certify' query requires one of six exact phrases, so it catches rebuttals and posts about other countries' elections that use them; its '38 million invalid' term catches replies asking for a source. The Texas query requires one of four exact phrases, so it catches news relays and defenders of the speaker. The Newsom query requires Newsom plus a death-penalty term or 'Newscum,' so it catches news relays and Newsom's defenders. The tax query requires Democrats, Dems or Neal plus a tax-cut or tax-hike phrase, so it also catches state-level tax stories and Democratic posts. The Michigan Wi-Fi query requires a Wi-Fi term plus Dominion, tabulator, 'voting machine' or 'Martin Township,' so it also catches rebuttals. The Somali query catches news relays, rebuttals and posts about the Minnesota fraud cases. The audit query catches posts mocking the demand. The 'fine people' query also catches posts defending the original reading. The Rikers query also catches straight news posts and rebuttals. The Medicare for All query catches supporters, opponents and general health-care posts, and its 'M4A' term can catch unrelated uses. The Van Hollen query catches syndicated news posts. Replies are included. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. This evening we pulled fresh samples for the 'do not certify,' Texas and Newsom queries; the other cards carry this morning's sentiment and say so. disinfo.caveatBody: New this evening: '38 million invalid voters, so the midterms can't be certified' misstates its own source. The figure comes from the group Unite4Freedom via Joe Hoft's blog, and Unite4Freedom describes the 38 million as 'registrations flagged for further investigation – not 38 million proven illegal registrations.' A flagged roll record (a move, a death, a data mismatch) is not a ballot cast illegally, and we found no official finding that any state's result is in doubt; Iowa's Republican secretary of state defended his state's results (WOWT), and leading 2020 election deniers including Cleta Mitchell and Michael Flynn accepted this year's results (Democracy Docket). We found no rated fact-check of the 38 million figure itself. 'Texas Democrats say the T stands for trans' turns one activist's gala speech into the incoming government's position; she said 'is for trans,' and the 'stands for' wording came from repost captions (The Watering Hole). Carried over from this morning: 'Newsom is letting killers go free' is false. The commutations would change 548 death sentences to life without the possibility of parole, and none has taken effect: the California Constitution requires the state Supreme Court to approve clemency for anyone with more than one felony conviction, and Newsom's office says it will wait for the court (The National News Desk). Trump's earlier figure of '563' death-row inmates does not match the 548 in the commutation; his new memorandum applies to federal cases and federal death sentences, not California's state death row (White House; AP). The Michigan Wi-Fi claim still has no official finding behind it: the voting system's federal certificate lists no wireless LAN or WAN (U.S. Election Assistance Commission), we found no reported result from the sheriff or CISA, and the bipartisan Board of State Canvassers certified Michigan's results on Nov. 23 (Michigan Department of State; Michigan Public). On the '95% on welfare' figure, KTTC found it 'needs context': Center for Immigration Studies data put Somali households in Minnesota receiving some form of welfare at 81%. 'Democrats are raising your taxes' is ahead of the facts: Rep. Richard Neal has announced hearings, not a bill, and any bill would face Trump's promised veto (POLITICO; X News).

The phrase was already common earlier in the week (14,472 posts on the UTC day of Nov 20), so its acceleration is real but smaller than the raw total suggests. The fuel is a Joe Hoft post, 'US ELECTIONS CANNOT BE CERTIFIED – Not With 38 Million Invalid Voters, No Chain of Custody for Mail-in Ballots, and Voter Machines Built for Fraud,' built on an interview with Harry Haury of the group Unite4Freedom (joehoft.com). X News summarized the push Tuesday afternoon ('Calls Grow to Withhold 2026 Midterm Election Certifications'): posters share 'DO NOT CERTIFY' graphics and call for Trump to order emergency audits, while election experts note no evidence of fraud that would change results. A separate X News story Tuesday described activists attacking Senate Republicans for adjourning without passing voter-ID and voter-roll measures. It builds on earlier calls: Kari Lake wrote 'Do not certify until you VERIFY the vote' about Iowa (Democracy Docket), and Iowa's Republican secretary of state, Paul Pate, defended the results as secure (WOWT).
talkingPoints: 38 million invalid voters means no honest certification is possible.
There's no chain of custody for mail-in ballots and the machines were built for fraud.
Governors and secretaries of state must not certify until every vote is verified.
Trump should declare an emergency and audit all 50 states.
Democrats stole America.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: Joe Hoft (joehoft.com) and Unite4Freedom's Harry Haury; @jjauthor (the most-engaged post in our sample); Kari Lake ('Do not certify until you VERIFY the vote,' earlier this month); activists such as Kevin Sorbo, Gunther Eagleman and Scott Presler, whom X News named in the related push against Senate Republicans; and many small accounts quote-posting Hoft.
narratives.whyItWorks: A huge round number sounds like an audit finding, and the article borrows the language of federal law (NVRA, HAVA) and accounting ('material' errors). It hands disappointed voters one concrete demand with a deadline — don't certify — as states finish their canvasses this month. It joins the Michigan Wi-Fi and forensic-audit claims into one story, and the size of the Democratic wave makes a stolen election feel plausible to people who never saw it coming.
narratives.audience: Trump voters stunned by the landslide; election-integrity activists; Republican county and state officials facing certification deadlines; low-trust voters who read messy voter rolls as proof of illegal votes.
narratives.counter: Use their own source. Unite4Freedom says the 38 million are records 'flagged for further investigation,' not proven illegal registrations, and a voter roll with people who moved or died is not a ballot cast illegally. Certification is a legal duty, not a vote of confidence, and Iowa's Republican secretary of state defended his state's results. Point out who isn't buying it: Cleta Mitchell, Michael Flynn and Stop the Steal's Ali Alexander all said this landslide was real (Democracy Docket).

Crime and punishment is one of the few issues where the Right still out-polls Democrats, and a lame-duck governor many see as a 2028 candidate is an easy national target. The 'he hid it until after the election' line turns a policy disagreement into a story about honesty. It also lets the Right change the subject from the midterm losses to Democrats and crime.

No one is being released: the sentences become life without parole, and the California Supreme Court must approve commutations for anyone with more than one felony, so none have taken effect. talkingPoints: A poll worker found a Chinese-made Wi-Fi radio broadcasting right next to a Dominion tabulator.
The machines are certified to have no wireless at all, so why is there a signal?
It kept broadcasting after the tabulator was locked away.
Michigan won't audit the machines, so CISA has to.
This is why every state needs a forensic audit before Democrats take power.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: Patrick Colbeck and the Election Crime Bureau (Mike Lindell-backed), @Joeoltmann (97,572 views on one post), @LindaRunstein, Badlands Media, Gateway Pundit (per replies in the sample), and Michigan state Rep. Rachelle Smit.
narratives.whyItWorks: It is concrete and technical: a named township, a named poll worker, a hardware address traced to Shenzhen, and a certification document that says 'no wireless.' That reads like evidence even though the hotspot's own name matches a consumer HDMI dongle and nothing shows a tabulator connected to anything. It also arrives as the audit demand is already rising and gives that demand a fresh 'smoking gun' and a China angle.
narratives.audience: 2020 election skeptics and Lindell followers; Michigan Republicans angry about the midterm losses; China hawks; and casual readers who see 'Dominion' and 'Chinese Wi-Fi' in the same sentence.
narratives.counter: Don't mock the poll worker. Say what the record shows: the hotspot's name matches a consumer wireless-display adapter, the tabulator model in use has no modem, and Michigan's tabulators are not connected to the internet while ballots are counted. If the sheriff is looking at it, let that finish and publish what it finds. Then point to Michigan's post-election audits and paper ballots, which can be hand-checked whatever a Wi-Fi scanner shows.

talkingPoints: Somalis have taken over Minnesota and Democrats let it happen.
Almost all of them are on welfare, paid for by your taxes.
Minnesota's fraud scandals prove it.
Deport them and clean up Minnesota first.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: Trump's Truth Social post (24,550 likes and 7,424 reposts by an archive's count on Monday afternoon), Laura Loomer (per X News), reply threads under @bennyjohnson and @WhiteHouse, and One America News.
narratives.whyItWorks: It ties two real things, Minnesota's large Somali community and the federal fraud prosecutions involving some of its members, to a false scale ('taken over,' '95%'). A round number from the president travels faster than a correction. It also recasts a blue state as foreign-controlled, which fits the 'Democrats import voters' story the Right has been pushing since the midterms.
narratives.audience: Trump's base and immigration hard-liners; Minnesotans angry about the fraud cases; and voters who already see Democratic states as mismanaged.
narratives.counter: Lead with the numbers: Somali Minnesotans are about 1 to 2 percent of the state, and most are U.S. citizens. Fraud should be prosecuted person by person, and it is. Using Medicaid or food aid is not the same as not working; most working-age Somali Minnesotans work. Don't argue in the abstract; name the nurses, drivers and small-business owners in the community.

factChecks.claim: 'Almost 95%' of Somalis in Minnesota 'are on some form of welfare.'
factChecks.detail: Center for Immigration Studies 2025 data show about 81% of Somali households in Minnesota receive some form of welfare (nearly 90% with children), with about 54% receiving food stamps and 73% with at least one member on Medicaid. High, and far above Minnesota-native households, but not 'almost 95%.' Trump provided no source.

factChecks.claim: 'Like 88%' of Somalis in Minnesota receive welfare (related Trump claim, Dec. 2025).
factChecks.detail: The White House gave FactCheck.org no evidence for the figure. Later data it added: 81% of Somali immigrant households (Center for Immigration Studies) and 84% of people reporting Somali ancestry (Minnesota state demographer) used some public assistance, mostly Medicaid. That is not the '95%' Trump posted on Nov. 22, 2026.

factChecks.claim: '92% [of Minnesota Somalis] don't work' (related Trump claim, Feb. 2026).
factChecks.detail: About 28% of Somalis in Minnesota aren't working, a smaller share than for Minnesotans overall; about 9 in 10 receive some public assistance, but those programs typically include low-wage workers.

X News summarized the plan Monday afternoon, noting it would also try to restore expired Affordable Care Act subsidies and reverse Medicaid cuts, and that Trump has said 'I'm going to veto them'; Democrats are short of the two-thirds needed to override. talkingPoints: Democrats ran on affordability and their first move is to take back your tax cut.
97% of filers got a tax cut; Democrats want to repeal it.
No tax on tips, overtime and Social Security is on the chopping block.
They haven't even been sworn in and they're already eyeing your paycheck.
Trump will veto it, so this is just a show.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: Rep. Lance Gooden (R-Texas), @GrassrootArmy, @Kencook22, @thisisjames_, sports-and-politics commentator @DavidPollackUSA (tying it to Obama's 'country club' line), and conservative sites such as Read The American and Conservative Daily News. Trump's 'I'm going to veto them' is the closing line.
narratives.whyItWorks: It turns the Democrats' winning word, affordability, against them at the start of tax season talk and right before Thanksgiving. 'Tax hike' is simpler than 'review of deficit-adding provisions,' and the popular pieces of the 2025 law (tips, overtime, Social Security) give the Right concrete things to say Democrats will take away. It also feeds the broader 'they lied to win' theme running through other Right cards this week.
narratives.audience: Middle-income workers who got the tips, overtime or senior deductions; small-business owners; fiscal conservatives; and swing voters who backed Democrats on costs but are wary of higher taxes.
narratives.counter: Be specific before the Right is. Say which provisions Democrats want to change, who pays (Neal has pointed to the parts Democrats say worsened the deficit), and that hearings are not a bill. Promise in plain words that tips, overtime and middle-class deductions are not the target, if that is the plan. Then put tariffs, which Neal also wants to review, back in the frame as the tax families are paying now.
